paths.description: UK consumer homepage: entry template, navigation, primary calls to action, preferences, performance and global policy checks.
PayPal Debit Card product-detail template: commercial product explanation, imagery and responsive layout.
Buy-now-pay-later product and FAQ template: regulated commercial copy, expandable guidance, metadata and no-JS delivery.
Send-money journey entry: core task explanation, CTA path, responsive layout and no-JS delivery.
Security and protection content template: trust claims, recovery guidance, responsive layout and no-JS delivery.

findings.summary: The public surface does not adapt to the user’s dark colour-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshots captured in default and prefers-color-scheme: dark are byte-identical at 63,512 bytes; the white page and blue hero remain unchanged.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and map page, component and browser-UI colours through light/dark tokens selected by prefers-color-scheme, following dark-mode guidance.

findings.summary: Navigating this MPA has no authored cross-document View Transition treatment.
findings.evidence: Rendered DOM/CSS evidence contains no @view-transition rule or view-transition-name despite prominent navigation between same-origin product pages.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a progressively enhanced cross-document view transition for stable header/hero elements, while preserving instant navigation under reduced motion.

findings.summary: The cookie interruption is implemented as fixed generic containers rather than a native dismissible top-layer primitive.
findings.evidence: DOM/evaluate evidence reports zero dialog and zero popover elements while showing .CookieBanner_container fixed above content with Accept, Decline and Close controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a semantically named dialog or appropriate popover with declarative controls, deterministic focus handling and platform dismissal semantics.

findings.summary: Cold mobile loading is far outside the recommended LCP range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured performance 0.57, FCP 8.2 s and LCP 12.1 s (CLS 0.033, TBT 0 ms). A separate unthrottled trace measured 546 ms LCP, showing the risk is network/device-sensitive rather than main-thread blocking.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP content and reduce its dependency chain; validate on Lighthouse mobile conditions and field CWV.

findings.summary: The entry page loads a large, fragmented critical network surface.
findings.evidence: HAR records 94 requests and 1,136,155 transferred bytes: 44 scripts (713,120 bytes), 19 stylesheets and multiple VeryHigh-priority parser-inserted stylesheets.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate and defer non-critical styles/scripts, explicitly prioritise only LCP-critical resources, and delay analytics and support code until needed or consented.

findings.summary: A substantial share of shipped JavaScript and CSS is unused on the homepage.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 231 KiB unused JavaScript and 30 KiB unused CSS; the component bundle is 53% unused and GTM is 64% unused.
findings.suggestedFix: Split page-specific components, conditionally import analytics/support modules and remove duplicated global/component CSS from the entry route.

findings.summary: Several visible control labels do not match their accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility found label-content-name-mismatch on the regional banner and carousel controls, including visible “Send” with aria-label “Go to page 1 of 4”.
findings.suggestedFix: Make each accessible name begin with and include its visible label, adding state or position after that label.

findings.summary: Heading and landmark structure is inconsistent on the homepage.
findings.evidence: The rendered page exposes two h1 elements for one phrase, then the cookie banner jumps from page h3 content to h4; Lighthouse flags heading-order. The evaluate probe found only a nav landmark and no main landmark.
findings.suggestedFix: Use one h1, keep heading levels structural rather than visual, give the cookie title an appropriate level, and expose a main landmark.

findings.summary: Some carousel pagination controls expose very small hit areas.
findings.evidence: The evaluate probe measured visible carousel indicator buttons as small as 8×8 CSS pixels, below a robust touch target, although all tested pages reflowed without horizontal overflow at 360 px.
findings.suggestedFix: Retain the small visual dot but provide at least a 44×44 CSS-pixel interactive hit area with adequate separation.

findings.summary: The homepage loses significant primary content when JavaScript is unavailable.
findings.evidence: Discoverability evidence reports 56% rendered-word coverage in raw HTML and no h1 in raw HTML, while the rendered page has two h1 elements. Detail routes retain 67–74% and their h1.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the complete hero heading and core homepage copy so the primary proposition survives without JavaScript.

findings.summary: Strong transport headers are weakened by permissive script policy and missing referrer policy.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence shows HSTS preload and nosniff, but CSP allows unsafe-inline for scripts/defaults and no Referrer-Policy header is present. CSP frame-ancestors mitigates the absent X-Frame-Options header.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unsafe-inline from script-src using the existing nonce strategy throughout and add a restrictive Referrer-Policy such as strict-origin-when-cross-origin.

findings.summary: Most homepage traffic is third-party or cross-origin telemetry and shared infrastructure.
findings.evidence: HAR attributes 84 of 94 requests and 1,032,165 of 1,136,155 bytes to third-party origins; tracker evidence finds GTM plus repeated Datadog and PayPal telemetry requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit each telemetry purpose, gate optional tags on consent, sample RUM, self-host or eliminate avoidable dependencies, and enforce a documented third-party budget.

findings.summary: Cookie policy is broader than needed and one telemetry cookie is not Secure.
findings.evidence: Cookie evidence found all 10 cookies flagged: nine SameSite=None and the first-party _dd_s telemetry cookie without Secure. Authentication-like cookies were HttpOnly and no sensitive client secret was found.
findings.suggestedFix: Set Secure on every cookie and use Lax or Strict unless a documented cross-site flow requires None; keep sensitive cookies HttpOnly.

findings.summary: The homepage cannot use the back/forward cache.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports three bfcache failure reasons, led by Cache-Control: no-store on the main resource and no-store responses requested by JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply no-store only to genuinely sensitive responses; separate cacheable public marketing HTML and telemetry requests from authenticated state.

findings.summary: Prominent imagery lacks intrinsic dimensions and modern negotiated formats.
findings.evidence: Image probes found the homepage hero JPEG oversized at 780 natural vs 351 displayed pixels with no width/height attributes; the debit-card JPEG also lacks dimensions and is not lazy despite being below the fold.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve AVIF/WebP candidates through picture/srcset, size candidates to rendered breakpoints, add width/height, and lazy-load non-critical below-fold images.

findings.summary: The page has no effective third-party byte/request budget.
findings.evidence: Third-party resources account for about 91% of transferred bytes, including 114,607 bytes for GTM and repeated background RUM calls; total load is 1.14 MB for a marketing entry page.
findings.suggestedFix: Set and enforce route-level budgets for total bytes, third-party bytes and request count; defer or sample background analytics after core content is stable.

taskList.title: Cut the cold-load critical path and unused route code
Harden CSP, referrer and cookie policy
Reduce and consent-gate telemetry and third-party dependencies
Repair accessible naming, heading landmarks and target sizes
Optimise image formats, dimensions and loading
Respect dark mode and use semantic dismissal primitives
Restore bfcache eligibility for public pages
